chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Improve your dwelling with the bounties of Allah, and beware lest they be transferred from you to others. Indeed, they have never been transferred from anyone except that they almost returned to him.' He said: 'And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: It is rare for something to turn away and then face you again.'

key_terms.تَنْتَقِلَ: to be transferred or moved away
key_terms.جِوَارَ: dwelling or vicinity; here metaphorically meaning to maintain a good relationship or status with

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'improve your dwelling' with Allah's bounties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs believers to cultivate gratitude and worthiness to retain Allah's bounties, warning that divine favors are transient and rarely return once lost. This concept of the fragility of blessings is reinforced by Imam Ali’s (AS) observation that what departs seldom returns, highlighting the need for constant spiritual vigilance. The narration underscores the Shia understanding of *ni'mah* not as a permanent right, but as a conditional trust requiring active maintenance through good conduct.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do good in the vicinity of the Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and be cautious of it being transferred away from you to others. But, it does not get transferred away from anyone at all so it almost never returns to him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Rare it is for something which turns away, so it faces you (again)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘You should keep good neighborly relations with the bounties of Allah, and guard them being transferred from you to others; if bounties transfer away from a person, they very rarely return. Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “It is very rare for something to come forward once it goes away.’””
